metadata.title: Rome Odunze goes for 94 yards in Week 4
metadata.description: Rome Odunze caught six of his seven targets for 94 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Odunze led the Bears in all receiving categories in what was his best game of the season. The veteran receiver has now caught 14 passes for 233 yards and no touchdowns through four games. Odunze will be a low-end WR3 in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Packers.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze - Season-best game with Bagent
metadata.description: Odunze caught six of seven targets for 94 yards in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards while finishing two targets shy of Colston Loveland's team-high total as Tyson Bagent threw for 268 yards. This was the first time Odunze exceeded 52 receiving yards in a game this season, as he showed nice chemistry with the third QB to start a game for the Bears this season. Odunze's outlook is unlikely to change significantly whether the Bears get Caleb Williams (hamstring) back or stick with Bagent for Week 5 at Green Bay.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze a Boom-Bust Week 4 Play
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is a volatile flex option in this Sunday's home matchup against the New York Jets. Odunze has put a preseason calf issue behind him, but still faces hurdles in the way of targets. Heading into the year, it seemed that this offense would funnel opportunities through Odunze, fellow wideout Luther Burden III, and tight end Colston Loveland in the passing game. Quarterback Caleb Williams' (hamstring) injury aside, it's veteran wide receiver Kalif Raymond standing in the way of Odunze's increased production. As it stands, the third-year pass catcher leads his cohorts in snaps. However, he's very clearly the main downfield threat in the attack, making easier looks harder to come by. Odunze is a talented young receiver, but his current standing in an offense loaded with weapons leaves something to be desired. Despite a tough spot in the Jets this weekend, the 24-year-old lands favorably as RotoBaller's PPR WR38.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze goes for 44 yards in Week 3
metadata.description: Rome Odunze caught three of his six targets for 44 yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Odunze finished third on the Bears in targets and receiving yards but he was unable to find the end zone for the third straight game. The veteran wideout has been outproduced by both Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond this season, catching just eight passes for 139 yards thus far through three games. He will be a fantasy flex option in Week 4 against the Jets.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze Has Another Quiet Game
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze didn't put up a huge game despite his team finding plenty of success against the visiting Eagles. With Case Keenum stepping in as the starting QB, Odunze caught three passes on six targets for a total of 44 receiving yards. Both Kalif Raymond and Luther Burden III had more catches, receiving yards, and targets than Odunze, and each found the end zone, while Odunze is still looking for his first score of the season. He only has eight catches in his first three games and seems to be playing a reduced role. While he leads the team in routes run, he only has a 14.4% target share, which caps his upside going forward in the short term, as the Bears take on the Jets in Week 4.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze - Three more catches in win
metadata.description: Odunze secured three of six targets for 44 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Odunze was relegated to a complementary role in the 20-point victory, finishing fourth in receptions and third in both receiving yards and targets for the Bears on the night. While Odunze entered the season as the presumptive No. 1 receiver, veteran offseason addition Kalif Raymond, who had familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's scheme from their mutual time with the Lions, has enjoyed an expanded role over the first three games while gathering in an impressive 19 of 21 targets. Conversely, Odunze is averaging a career-best 17.4 yards per reception but has a modest eight catches and no touchdowns through three games, numbers he'll look to significantly boost during a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze Boasts Increased Risk Sans QB1
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze will line up against staunch opposition in the visiting Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 3. Despite a scoring outburst in the team's road opener, Chicago's passing offense has begun the season cold. Preseason injuries to Odunze and teammate Luther Burden III may have contributed to the slow start. Either way, the offense takes a hit as long as quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) is sidelined. The silver lining for Odunze is that he appears to be over the calf injury that plagued him after seeing his snap share nearly double to 84% in Week 2. Still, it's challenging to project a productive day for Chicago's attack in the wake of Williams' soft-tissue ailment. Moreover, Philadelphia's defensive squad has stifled opposing passing attacks to the tune of 166 yards per game - the fifth-best mark in the league. Among a few cons in his profile, the third-year pro takes a dip in value, falling to RotoBaller's PPR WR49 preceding their second home outing.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze's Value in Question Amid Quarterback Uncertainty in Chicago
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze has had an underwhelming start to the 2026 season, recording five catches for 95 yards on seven targets across his team's first two games. The 24-year-old entered the year battling a calf injury, which may explain some of his struggles. However, Odunze now projects to be impacted by a different injury in the games to come. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and his return timeline is currently unclear. For as long as Odunze is catching passes from Bears backup quarterbacks Tyson Bagent (concussion) and/or Case Keenum, it may be difficult for him to provide consistent fantasy production. Even in the best circumstances, Odunze is not guaranteed to see a high volume of targets in a Chicago offense that also features wide receiver Luther Burden III and tight end Colston Loveland. Between his slow start and the Bears' quarterback questions, Odunze profiles outside the top-48 at wide receiver for fantasy managers entering Week 3.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze catches three passes in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Rome Odunze caught three of his four targets for 43 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Odunze has struggled to make an impact in a slow-starting Chicago passing attack to begin the season, finishing with three receptions or less in each of the first two games. The pass-catcher remains difficult to trust with the potential absence of quarterback Caleb Williams ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze - Three grabs in Sunday's loss
metadata.description: Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: The 2024 first-round pick led all Bears wideouts in receiving yards on a wet and windy day at Soldier Field. Odunze has had a slow start to the season, managing just a 5-95-0 line on seven targets through two games, and his outlook in the short term won't be improved if the hamstring injury that knocked Caleb Williams out of Sunday's contest proves to be serious. Odunze could be catching passes from Tyson Bagent instead in a Week 3 home tilt against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze Eyes More Impactful Week 2 Outing
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is set to resume his typical role in the team's offense when they line up for a divisional bout with the visiting Minnesota Vikings in Week 2. Odunze dealt with a calf issue for a week or so leading up to Chicago's road opener against Carolina. He was active - despite three straight limited practice sessions - but ranked third regarding snap counts (49%) at his position and hauled in just two-of-three targets for 52 yards. Uninspiring debut aside, the third-year wideout projects as, at worst, a 1B option in Chicago's receiving corps alongside teammate Luther Burden III. More importantly, quarterback Caleb Williams looked improved, even if it was a small sample. Minnesota's defense poses a threat, but Chicago's attack will be difficult to stop if it's firing on all cylinders. Odunze is RotoBaller's PPR WR35 and should continue trending up the further removed he is from an early-season soft-tissue issue.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze an Occasional Bust Candidate in Crowded Offense
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze has plenty of talent, but his exact volume could fluctuate from week to week due to the crowded state of the offense. Although the Bears dropped 59 points last week, Odunze and tight end Colston Loveland combined for two catches. Between Luther Burden III, Odunze, Kalif Raymond, and Cole Kmet, there are a lot of reliable targets for Caleb Williams in Chicago. They all have relatively high ceilings, but we also wouldn't be surprised to see them naturally alternate which players have big games or quiet games. For that reason, there's a decent chance that Odunze is a top-18 fantasy receiver going forward, but there's also a chance that he's a low-end RB3/flex or worse. The 24-year-old belongs on the bench in most leagues for now, especially as he recovers from a calf injury. He should be active this week, but Burden is currently the only must-start fantasy receiver in Chicago.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze (calf) off injury report for Week 2
metadata.description: Rome Odunze (calf) carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Odunze has been recovering from a calf injury for a while, but it seems that he is fully over it at this point, as he isn't listed on Chicago's injury report at all heading into Week 2. It's likely that his workload will ramp up this week after he was limited in the season opener, which should help him to produce a fantasy finish better than his underwhelming performance in Week 1.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze quiet in Week 1
metadata.description: Rome Odunze caught two of his three targets for 52 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers
metadata.analysis: Odunze made the most of minimal usage in the Chicago passing attack in the season opener, averaging 26.0 yards per reception in the win. the wideout provides head coach Ben Johnson with one of many dynamic pass-catching options ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze - Little volume in Week 1 rout
metadata.description: Odunze caught two of three targets for 52 yards in Sunday's 59-37 win over the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: In the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history, Odunze didn't get much of a chance to contribute, with Kalif Raymond (8-84-0 on nine targets) and Luther Burden (5-63-0 on five targets) getting more looks from Caleb Williams and the ground game accounting for six of the Bears' eight TDs. Better days should be ahead for Odunze, perhaps as soon as Week 2 at home against the Vikings.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze (calf) active for Week 1
metadata.description: Rome Odunze (calf) is officially active for Week 1 for the Chicago Bears against the Carolina Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Odunze is good to go after passing through pregame testing without any setbacks from the calf injury, offering head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catching option for quarterback Caleb Williams against the Panthers Sunday.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze - Ready to go for Week 1
metadata.description: Odunze (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Despite being a limited participant throughout Week 1 prep while managing the calf injury that first cropped up Sept. 3, Odunze has received the green light to play in the Bears' season opener. Odunze should handle his usual starting role, and the Bears haven't provided any indication that he'll have his snaps limited as a result of the injury.

metadata.title: Rome Odunze Officially Active for Week 1
metadata.description: Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze (calf) is officially active for the team's Week 1 season opener on Sunday versus the Carolina Panthers, according to the team. Odunze was limited in practice all week due to a knee injury that surfaced in early September, but he did enough on the field to gain clearance to play in the season opener this weekend. There have not been any reports floating around that the 24-year-old former first-rounder will not have his typical number of offensive snaps for the Bears on Sunday, so fantasy managers should keep him in their starting lineups to kick off the year. Odunze only played in 12 regular-season games a year ago due to a foot injury that is believed to be behind him, but durability issues have been a bit of a concern. He caught 44 of 90 targets last year for 661 yards and a career-high six touchdowns in his second season in the NFL. With DJ Moore now in Buffalo, Odunze and Luther Burden III will operate as Chicago's top two wideouts in 2026. At the very least, Odunze should be a solid WR3/flex option for fantasy managers in Week 1.
